text: When the seventh month came, and the Israelites were settled in their towns, the people gathered as one in Jerusalem.

Then Jeshua son of Jozadak and his fellow priests, together with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and his kinsmen, set to work and rebuilt the altar of the God of Israel, to offer burnt offerings on it as prescribed in the Law of Moses, the man of God.
They set the altar on its foundations, for they were in dread of the peoples of the surrounding lands, and they offered burnt offerings on it to the LORD, both morning and evening offerings.

versions.text: They set the altar on its foundations, for they were afraid of the peoples around them, and they offered burnt offerings on it to the LORD, both morning and evening offerings.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew reads "the peoples of the lands" (עַמֵּי הָאֲרָצוֹת), a fixed expression in Ezra–Nehemiah for the surrounding non-exilic populations; "the peoples around them" loses that. "Dread was upon them" is also stronger than a simple "were afraid," and the phrase reads well aloud.

text: They celebrated the Festival of Booths as it is written, offering the daily burnt offerings by number, as the ordinance required for each day,

versions.text: They celebrated the Festival of Booths as it is written, offering the required number of burnt offerings day by day,
versions.explanation: The clause כְּמִשְׁפַּט ("according to the ordinance/regulation") is not represented; the translation collapses "by number" and "as prescribed for each day" into a single phrase, losing the emphasis that both the count and the daily schedule followed the law.

text: and after that the regular daily offerings, the offerings for the new moons and for all the appointed festivals of the LORD, as well as the freewill offerings brought to the LORD.
From the first day of the seventh month they began to offer burnt offerings to the LORD, though the foundation of the LORD's temple had not yet been laid.

They gave money to the masons and carpenters, and food, drink, and oil to the people of Sidon and Tyre, so that they would ship cedar logs from Lebanon by sea to Joppa, as authorized by Cyrus king of Persia.

In the second month of the second year after their arrival at the house of God in Jerusalem, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak, along with the rest of their kinsmen—the priests and the Levites and all who had come back from captivity to Jerusalem—began the work, and they appointed Levites twenty years old and upward to supervise the building of the house of the LORD.

So Jeshua with his sons and kinsmen, and Kadmiel with his sons, the descendants of Judah, stood together to oversee those working on the house of God, along with the sons of Henadad with their sons and kinsmen, the Levites.

When the builders had laid the foundation of the temple of the LORD, the priests took their places in their vestments with trumpets, and the Levites, the sons of Asaph, with cymbals, to praise the LORD according to the directions of David king of Israel.

And they sang responsively, praising and giving thanks to the LORD: "He is good; his steadfast love toward Israel endures forever." Then all the people raised a great shout of praise to the LORD, because the foundation of the house of the LORD had been laid.

But many of the priests and Levites and heads of families, the old men who had seen the first house, wept aloud when they saw the foundation of this house being laid, while many others shouted for joy.
No one could distinguish the sound of the shouts of joy from the sound of weeping, for the people raised such a great shout that the noise was heard far away.
